Affiliation:: School of Electrical and Computer Engineering, University of Oklahoma
Data & Platforms: OASIS (Open Access Series of Imaging Studies)
Application Areas: Intelligent Energy Systems and Smart Grids
Key Research Thinking Patterns: Hybrid Generative-Boosting Frameworks for Inverse Design: Combining physics-based simulations with hybrid generative models to accelerate photonic component design, exemplified by the XG-Attention-WGAN PIC framework that uses FDTD data and Wasserstein GANs to autonomously discover microring resonator geometries with high Q-factor performance.

Transfer Learning and Region-Based Detection for Medical Imaging: Leveraging pre-trained deep architectures and region-based convolutional neural networks for precise segmentation and classification of complex medical data, demonstrated by Fast R-CNN achieving 99% accuracy in glioma, meningioma, and pituitary tumor classification from MRI scans.

Hierarchical Transformer Learning for Unlabeled Data Synthesis: Applying hierarchical transformer networks with positive-unlabeled learning strategies to predict synthesizability of hypothetical materials, specifically using the SyntheFormer model to filter thermodynamically stable but unrealized structures and prioritize experimental targets.

Bibliometric and Taxonomic Mapping of AI Trajectories: Utilizing topic modeling, text mining, and co-occurrence mapping to synthesize large-scale literature landscapes, such as analyzing 783 papers to map the evolution of machine learning applications in Alzheimer’s disease research and identify shifts toward multimodal data integration.
Summary Description: Mike Banad is a researcher specializing in the intersection of artificial intelligence, computational engineering, and biomedical sciences. His work focuses on developing advanced machine learning frameworks for three primary domains: smart grid resilience, photonic integrated circuit design, and medical diagnostics. He employs hybrid architectures, such as combining Wasserstein GANs with XGBoost for inverse design in photonics, and hierarchical transformers for materials discovery. In healthcare, he utilizes transfer learning and region-based CNNs for high-accuracy brain tumor classification and applies bibliometric analysis to track AI trends in neurodegenerative disease research. His methodology emphasizes robustness through cross-dataset validation, uncertainty quantification, and the integration of IoT and edge computing infrastructures.
